author: Akien
prose: A device that knows what's important for Claude Code to know about X as it works on Y. Born from CC violating the ground loop boundary 3x in one day — memory doesn't stick, flags are policy, this is physics. Builds bodies of knowledge per project by mining structural patterns, learning from corrections, and type-checking proposed changes. Graph tree paths ARE the type system. A component's intention becomes its positive type (what it IS), corrections become negative types (what it ISN'T), and proposed changes are type-checked — unification with a positive type means it fits, with a negative type means rejection, match with neither means novel (surface for a ruling). Six question dimensions seed the initial trees: boundary (where does this thing end), ownership (whose concern does this serve), direction (which way does the dependency point), scope of change (same vs. new responsibility), correction history (what's been pushed back on), and intent alignment (does this serve what the component is FOR). The six core values (CP1-CP6) are the lens — they don't add dimensions, they color every path with WHY a pattern matters. Five capabilities: (1) mine — scan a codebase and derive the initial pattern lattice, cold start; (2) review and learn — take input, identify patterns, learn from corrections; (3) challenge — adversarial check, actively challenge proposed changes against the type system; (4) answer query — what matters about X while working on Y; (5) digest — nighttime/batch mode, process corrections into updated type definitions, notice which error classes die off. Pre-learning: universal pattern catalog (GOF, SOLID, architectural smells) as vocabulary, seeded by LLM reading pattern references. Project-specific patterns from mining + Akien's corrections layer on top. Runs on Hex (M1 Studio 32GB, ollama) for the batch/digest work. Interactive mode is retrieval against what digest already computed. Not project-specific — builds a KB for any codebase, with universal patterns as base and project patterns layered on. Boris Cherny's constraint approach: make the illegal state unrepresentable, don't detect it after. Akien: 'it's job is to know what's important for you to know about x as you work on y.' And: 'it can't be a code reasoner JUST FOR THIS PROJECT. It becomes a key part of our workflow. so it needs to be able to build that kind of KB for any codebase.' [ENRICHED 2026-08-30, same conversation] THE DEEPER WHY (Akien verbatim): A no list is part of what we're building. But a huge part of what we've learned is: it does not matter what we do it will be wrong. And what's making it wrong right now is too many things in your head. Or not enough. Or the wrong things. Constantly. There are too many things is part of the problem. The complexity limit. Just because yours is higher than aider's doesn't mean it's not there. That's what this very specific repeating error type is. My brain has the same problem. The reason my brain works the way it does is to manage that problem. Temporary working memory. Inner narrative. Competing activations... it's all about managing from moment to moment which context is most important. We know your internal cognition has loops in it. But we can't easily inspect and tune them. But in something you and I build, we can. So we don't start by trying to build a builder. We start by trying to build a robot we can improve who does things for you. And you and I learn from that.
